description.p: mb3d-rs is Mandelbulb3D (MB3D), the 3D fractal program, rewritten so that it runs on today's computers: on Linux, Windows and macOS, and with the picture calculated on the graphics card where MB3D could only use the processor. It opens MB3D's parameter files (.m3p, .m3i, text parameters from forums), uses MB3D's formulas and maps, and makes the same pictures.

The windows are MB3D's own: the main window, Formulas, Lighting, Post processing, Navigator, Animation, Batch, Big renders, Monte Carlo, Voxel export, Bulb Tracer 2, MutaGen and the rest. If you know MB3D, you know this program, and MB3D's tutorials apply.

ul.li: Ray marching, shadows, ambient occlusion and reflections on the graphics card (Vulkan), with the processor's cores sharing the work
MB3D's formulas, including the hundreds written in machine code, run on the card and on the processor
Monte Carlo path tracing with a neural noise filter (Intel Open Image Denoise, on the processor in this package)
Animations, big tiled renders, voxel and mesh export, a swarm of computers sharing one picture
Interfaces in several languages, themes, and the mb3d command line renderer for scripts (flatpak run --command=mb3d io.github.thr32423.mb3d-rs)

description.p: MutaGen shows the variation you sent to the main window in its centre when you come back, and its generation arrows point left and right. The Navigator's arrow buttons keep moving while held. The AI window explains how to install and connect Claude Code on Windows, with a command that works in PowerShell and Command Prompt.

Your settings and files from an earlier version can be brought over from any folder: from the start-up question, from a question on a new copy's first start, or later from the Folders window (Prefs, Ini Dirs). Afterwards the program asks you to start it again instead of restarting itself.

A new version unpacked next to the one used before offers to bring over your settings, History, saved parameters, maps, Big renders and meshes, which each copy keeps in its own folder. MutaGen closes when it sends a picture to the main window. A map chosen by its picture shows the picture's name with its number. 61 new maps by Geoffrey N. Barnes (10001 to 13015). A scene whose maps do not fit the graphics card is calculated on the processor instead.

The Navigator shows the fog and depth colours as the main window does, and one switch, "Main window's look", gives the main window's lighting and, when the camera rests, its full picture; a drag on the view looks around or slides. A map or a background picture is chosen from a grid of the folder's pictures (a click on its small picture in the Lighting window). MutaGen keeps its generations when it is opened again. A stopped calculation no longer waits for a shader the graphics card still compiles, and a picture whose formula overflows on the card has its shadows and reflections from the processor too.

Other programs can use the engine (experimental): mb3d serve gives a program in any language pictures over lines of JSON: it opens a parameter file or a formula, changes settings and a formula's own values, and renders the picture with its depth, with progress and stop. The same is there as a small Rust library (mb3d::api). docs/API.md describes both.

Opening an old .m3i no longer freezes the program: the picture shows at once, and reflections, clouds and depth of field follow in the background with progress and Stop. File previews leave out the reflections, appear in about two seconds and stop when the dialog closes or another file is clicked. JosKn-KleinIFS, JosKn-ModIFS, SinePowSum, SurfBox, diamondIFS and eiffieCarIFS now run on the graphics card.

Position and rotation can be saved and loaded in files of their own, to bring a view to another scene. Panels that open and close come back at their place. On closing, every window goes at once and a shader still compiling is finished in the background, so the next start of that scene does not compile it again.

Safer and easier to use: damaged or hostile files and swarm jobs end in an error instead of a crash or a hang; parameter files are saved so that a full disk keeps the old file, and failed saves are reported. In the main window Ctrl+O, Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Shift+S, F5 and Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y open, save, calculate and undo. File dialogs and windows open where they were left, the five-minute History copy keeps every change, and the command line names a mistyped option with the one meant.

The Droste effect: the picture repeated in itself as in Escher's Print Gallery, along Escher's spiral or as concentric copies, with a window that shows it live on the calculated picture (the centre set by a click, the radii by the mouse wheel) and a phase that, animated from 0 to 1, makes an endless zoom from one calculated picture. Saved with the parameters, in all 18 interface languages.

Twelve wishes of the Mandelbulb Maniacs group: 360 photos that Facebook recognises, maps of any name, a colour picker with a hex field and an eyedropper, errors explained in plain words, a Share window, Mandelbulber settings files opening, a Formula book that explains every formula and its values, own step settings for the passes after the main one and a noise doctor, background pictures shown 1:1, texture export (height, normal and occlusion maps), mesh export without flying parts and decimated, and a benchmark with a result to post. Tamil as the 18th interface language.

The background picture's load options of the Lighting window (smooth on load, rows scaled to a geographic projection, left and right borders fitted) work as in Mandelbulb3D, so scenes saved with them and their 360 panoramas look as there. Reflections shared between the graphics card and the processor finish sooner on small pictures (20 to 38 % on the reflection stage at a quarter size), the command line keeps the shaders of long compiles for the next run, and a render stopped and continued is proven to equal the uninterrupted one.

Two objects side by side render faster on the processor: both parts of a DE combination are now compiled into functions of their own when a picture starts (before only the first part was, the second called its formulas one by one). Such scenes take up to 27 % less time, the pictures the same to the bit.

Saving a picture no longer freezes the window. The picture file is now written on a background thread: a 16 bit colour or OpenEXR save of a big picture takes a few seconds, and the window stays live while it is written, showing "Saving" until the file is done, as the original Mandelbulb3D did.

Animation templates: a 360 degree orbit around the fractal on any axis and a fly-through, made from the current view in one step; 360 degree photos and 360 degree VR animations, mono and stereo, for VR headsets and 360 video players (by Rathinagiri S, SRathinaGiri). The malware scan the README points to (scanrepo.dev) reads the repository as safe again: two math functions of the formula compiler were named eval, a word the scanner takes for running hidden code; they are renamed, and a test keeps the name from coming back.

Water as a ray tracer sees it. The sea of the ground plane is now traced from the eye to the exact surface of its waves: the water reaches the bottom edge of the picture with a camera low over it (no more dark band), and it meets the sky at the horizon without a line, also in Monte Carlo renders and on the graphics card. Its mirror rays leave the water like a ray tracer's. The waves run along the wind instead of crossing it from both sides, and the clouds reach the horizon, fading evenly into the sky. The Pascal formulas give the same results on macOS as elsewhere. A new example scene: sunset at sea.

Faster formulas. The formulas written in Pascal (MB3D's JIT formulas, 72 of them among MB3D's and the community's) are now compiled to machine code: three to four times faster on the processor, with the same results, and most of them now also run on the graphics card. The community's formulas in machine code run as compiled code too instead of being interpreted (up to 18 times faster). Scenes slightly above the single precision limit stay on the graphics card's faster calculation. A fix: the program crashed when the Save window was pulled to a very small size.

Transparent water: the ground plane's water can be see-through, so a fractal standing half in it shows beneath the surface, bent by the refraction and turning turquoise and then into the water's colour with depth. New settings on the Cutting page: Water (transparency), Absorption (how murky), the deep water colour, Refraction and Scattering, which makes the water glow towards the sun, lets wave crests shine through, casts light shafts cut by the fractal's shadows and gives submerged parts a soft glow; Monte Carlo traces the light through the water. It shows in the normal render with the reflections on, and in Monte Carlo. The waves are now an irregular sea instead of three regular waves, so scenes with waves look different. A fix: reflections on the processor that met the water were coloured like the fractal.

The program behaves more like the original Mandelbulb3D. Saving over an existing file asks first; a file dropped during a render no longer stops it; Stop asks after 15 minutes of rendering; "Save image in m3i" stores the finished picture. Post processing: "Reset now" keeps hand-calculated shadows, depth of field strengthens with each press, each "Calculate now" runs only its own step. Formula lists are sorted by vote and open when the mouse rests on a button; built-in formulas have descriptions; the animation preview shows frames as they render. Dialogs no longer change the folders of the settings. Five places now follow MB3D's rules: a negative Min R in Amazing Box and Bulbox, the dynamic fog's far offset, ambient shadows seen from inside, inside and outside scenes, and formula combinations. Every graphics card shader is checked in the tests without a card.

129 more formulas, 154 more maps and 608 light presets from the Mandelbulb3D community, taken from the free Mandelbulb3D 1.99.37 package by Machina Infinitum, each formula credited to its author (CREDITS-community.md in the formula, map and light folders); the Lighting window's quick load list opens the new M3Lights folder. The example scenes are gone; mb3d --save-scene writes a scene file from any parameters.

Batches no longer use more and more memory with every file, and when the graphics card meets many new formula combinations at once, its shader compiles wait while memory is short instead of filling it; a batch says first how many combinations are new. Parameters pasted with lines cut off in copying are refused with a message instead of calculating the wrong scene. 360 degree panoramas leave out the vignette and the colour fringes, which darkened the view behind the viewer. The experimental speed-ups' combined gains were measured again. The release no longer carries the examples folder.

Clouds in the program are no longer painted black: every calculation set their colour back to black, which made them dark and a dense cloud layer turned the sky black. The cloud density and coverage boxes show their values plainly (0.7, not 0.69999). A new page shows clouds, water and reflections in three pictures with their parameters to paste in.

The cone march no longer loses thin parts of formulas whose distance estimate is far too large, and it is faster: the march about a fifth shorter on the processor and a tenth on the graphics card, also in scenes with dynamic fog. The Navigator keeps the main window's view when it opens, its axes stay sharp, and on Windows the main window can now cover it.

Cone march, a new experimental speed-up: a coarse ray per block of pixels starts every pixel's march, which makes the march up to 60 % faster in open scenes, on the processor and the graphics card. Internal tab, Experimental..., or cone_march = on.

Gaussian splats: the fractal exported as a splat file, to look at from every side in Blender 5.3 and other splat viewers. The Bulb Tracer window has a Gaussian splats button, and the command line has mb3d splat.
The experimental speed-ups are kept from one start of the program to the next.

Experimental speed-ups that can be switched on one by one: longer march steps, a secant search for the surface, no step limit without dynamic fog, and DE ambient occlusion at half resolution. They change the picture a little and are off by default.
Scenes that need double precision are calculated on the graphics card again, and long texts in Japanese and Chinese wrap properly.
Finishing for every picture: exposure, glow around bright light, filmic tone mapping, contrast, saturation, warmth, a vignette and colour fringes.
A fine surface relief (rough, stone or grain) with colour variation, fixed to the fractal. A turntable animation in one click, recording a flight in the Navigator, and motion blur for animations.

Ideas from Mandelbulber: a ground plane or water under the fractal, volumetric clouds that cast shadows and show in reflections, surface materials (Fresnel, iridescence, glow), two fractals in one scene, a fisheye camera and 360 degree stereo panoramas for VR, OpenEXR pictures and HDR backgrounds that light Monte Carlo renders, animation curves to see and drag keyframes, and Catmull-Rom interpolation through every keyframe.
A swarm now calculates exactly the same picture as one computer. A crash is reported at the next start, and the Navigator can match the main window's lighting.

Five new interface languages: Spanish, Portuguese, Indonesian, Arabic and Urdu, seventeen in all. Arabic and Urdu are written right to left, with their letters joined and Latin words and numbers in the right order. The README and the wiki are translated into the new languages too.

AI assistants can use the program: connect Claude's desktop app or Claude Code with the new AI button on the Prefs tab, then ask in plain words, or by voice through the assistant, to describe, change and render your pictures, make variations, preview a folder or render what you worked on last; the assistant sees the pictures and can adjust them. The program stays offline, writes only into its AI folder, never deletes anything and asks before pictures larger than 4K.

A log of everything the program does, with a Log window behind the title bar's page icon: every click and setting, calculations with their stages and times, files, messages, warnings and errors, and a session that froze or was killed reported at the next start; while the graphics card's shaders compile, the status line shows a ticking clock and gently pulses; the History window handles histories of any size and groups them by day; the README and the wiki in all twelve languages of the program; smoother Navigator and drop-down lists.

The History window behind the title bar's clock icon: every picture calculated with its thumbnail and every file opened or saved, as a list, rows or tiles; a lighting change only repaints, as in Mandelbulb3D; a formula that never returns no longer slows a render to a crawl.
Safe Rust throughout except the C library and the JIT, a card listed twice in a Flatpak sandbox counted once, the files of the Flatpak.
